title: Bosehedral: Compiler Optimization for Bosonic Quantum Computing
problem: Bosonic quantum computing lacks effective compiler optimizations and faces the challenge of handling infinite-dimensional qumode gate matrices, limiting the performance of boson sampling on quantum hardware.
motivation: Bosonic quantum computing shows promise for practical applications that are classically hard, but requires compiler optimizations to reach its full potential.
method: Bosehedral optimizes quantum programs by representing quantum operations with compact, finite matrices instead of infinite-dimensional ones. It then breaks down these compact representations into simpler operations the hardware can execute, maps the high-level logical operations to physical ones the hardware supports, and uses tunable probabilistic gate dropout—randomly removing operations in a controlled way—to reduce gate counts while maintaining accuracy.
key_novelty: Bosehedral enables bosonic quantum program optimization by replacing infinite-dimensional matrices with compact representations.
contributions: Bosehedral compiler optimization framework for bosonic quantum computing
Tunable probabilistic gate dropout method for performance-fidelity tradeoff

metrics.other: significant program size reduction and end-to-end performance improvement
